questions.question: With `--exclude-ext=log`, are the files `a.log`, `catalog`, `.log` and `A.LOG` excluded?
questions.reference: matchesExt (src/filter.zig): for an extension without a leading dot, the name must be longer than ext+1 and have a '.' right before the extension. So `a.log` is excluded; `catalog` is not (no dot before `log`); `.log` is not (length 4 is not > 4); `A.LOG` is not (case-sensitive comparison).

questions.question: Which directories does zgrep skip by default? Are `dist` or `build` among them?
questions.reference: default_excluded_dirs (src/filter.zig): .git, .zig-cache, __pycache__, node_modules, .venv, venv, target, .cache, .idea, .vscode. Neither dist nor build is in the list. --no-ignore or --no-default-ignore disable the list.

questions.question: In a `--queries-file`, what values may "id" take, what happens with unknown fields, duplicate ids and blank lines, and can a bad line leave the batch half-run?
questions.reference: parseQueries (src/batch.zig): id is a string or a non-negative integer; unknown fields are rejected; a duplicate id is an error; blank lines are ignored. The whole file is parsed before anything runs (fails closed), so a bad line never leaves a batch half-run.

questions.question: Which event types count as results for `--max-results`? Do context lines count?
questions.reference: isResult (src/batch.zig): match, occurrence, file and count events. Context, passthru, provenance, query_end and summary do not count.

questions.question: What values does `--encoding` accept, and what does `--encoding=utf-16` do with a file that has no BOM?
questions.reference: parseEncoding (src/scan.zig): auto, none, utf-8, utf-16, utf-16le, utf-16be, latin1. auto = BOM sniff only (default); utf-16le/be decode ignoring any BOM; utf-16 lets the BOM decide and falls back to little-endian (like rg); utf-8/latin1 use the bytes as they are.

questions.question: What makes a directory tree a "micro-tree" in zgrep, and what changes when it is one?
questions.reference: Its regular files add up to less than 2 MB (micro_tree_max_bytes = 2*1024*1024 in src/main.zig) and the discovery stays within 2048 files, 512 directories and depth 32 (tryQuickTreeScan, src/kamikaze.zig). It is scanned on the calling thread: no worker pool, no io_uring, and no .gitignore/.dataignore inspection. --force-swarm disables the micro path.

questions.question: Does zgrep accept `--binary-files=binary`? What do `text` and `without-match` do?
questions.reference: No: `binary` is rejected at parse time with a usage error, because zgrep cannot print matches while suppressing binary content (BinaryFiles in src/main.zig). `text` is exactly -a; `without-match` is the default (a binary file is treated as not matching).

questions.question: Which options make zgrep use the sorted (ordered) path even when `--sort` is not given?
questions.reference: --exec, --heading and --pre each set opts.sort = true in runSearch (src/main.zig): exec needs to know which files matched, heading groups would interleave in completion order, and --pre runs per file.
